Iran is calling it a win-win deal, but to me it seems like they're calling it that because they won twice. Am I wrong?

There is no ELI5 version of this deal, if anyone does actually provide one then it will be heavily biased in one way or another.

This deal is a great opportunity for the west to move forward with the east towards greater cooperation and understanding, or it will be used as an example of a failure of diplomacy and a reason to drop bombs and start wars. Only time will tell.

Or... you know, it will fall in the middle and be used by both sides to further confuse geopolitics in order to further personal selfish goals by whoever is involved at the time.

An excellent point. Geopolitics has no ELI5; it's the most complex system on Earth. Several hundred million (or billions in some cases) people being represented by (in this deal) maybe 50 diplomats trying to find common ground where every side losses something while also gaining something else.

True negotiation has no winners, but nor does it have losers. It has compromise as it's victory. So in a sense the deal haters are right the West didn't make its best deal, but Iran also didn't make its best deal. The two sides made concessions were they felt safe to, & held fast in others.

Tl;Dr - in geopolitics you can't have your cake & eat it. No deal is perfect
